subject.title: fix(msteams): avoid memory spikes from oversized certificate files

question: Should Microsoft Teams federated authentication establish a 64 KiB certificate-file ceiling for existing installations?
rationale: The patch intentionally turns a previously unbounded accepted input into a startup failure, and repository evidence does not establish whether deployed PEM certificate/key bundles above 64 KiB must remain compatible.

options.title: Confirm 64 KiB and share the reader
options.body: Approve the 64 KiB boundary, replace the custom implementation with `readSecretFileSync`, preserve existing link behavior explicitly, and add upgrade-focused coverage.

options.title: Choose a larger compatibility cap
options.body: Select a higher bounded limit based on realistic certificate-chain fixtures, then use the shared reader with tests around that boundary.

options.title: Pause the hard ceiling
options.body: Do not merge until Microsoft Teams ownership can establish a safe deployed-certificate compatibility boundary.

recommendation.title: Confirm 64 KiB and share the reader
recommendation.body: Approve the 64 KiB boundary, replace the custom implementation with `readSecretFileSync`, preserve existing link behavior explicitly, and add upgrade-focused coverage.
